title: Distance Plus Angle: Polar Form Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
A ship radios: we are 5 km out, at 37 degrees. No east, no north, just a distance and an angle, and that is enough to find it. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (Chapter 4, Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations) we write complex numbers the same way: the polar form z = r(cos theta + i sin theta). The polar form is not in the current NCERT text; the JEE Main syllabus lists the modulus and the argument it is built from.

You will see the polar form derived from one right angled triangle, then turn two live dials (theta counts up, then r grows) while z, its mirror z bar and both forms update every frame. We compare Cartesian and polar form side by side, see why multiplying by i is a quarter turn, write 1 + root 3 i in polar form, and fix the trap of a negative r. Two pause-and-think questions, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 A ship gives a distance and an angle
0:32 Note: beyond the current NCERT text, in JEE
0:44 Deriving z = r(cos theta + i sin theta)
1:31 Live: two dials, r and theta
1:54 Pause and think: adding 2 pi
2:12 Cartesian form vs polar form
2:23 Multiplying: the r's multiply, the angles add
2:43 Pause and think: is it polar form?
3:13 Worked example: 1 + root 3 i
3:40 Exam trap: r is never negative
4:01 Where it is asked
4:12 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:42 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 45): Quadratic Equations with Real and Complex Roots. A ball thrown up reaches some heights twice, and some never.
